question: Olympic bronze medallist boxer Vijender Singh hails from which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vijender Singh (विजेंदर सिंह) hails from Kaluwas village, Bhiwani district, Haryana.

• He won the bronze medal in the middleweight (75 kg) category at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, becoming India's first-ever Olympic medallist in boxing.

• He was awarded the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2009) and the Padma Shri (2010).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bhiwani in Haryana is often called the 'Little Cuba' of India for producing many top boxers.

• Vijender turned professional in 2015 and later entered politics.

NOTE

• Odisha (Option 1): An eastern coastal state known for the Sun Temple at Konark and Jagannath Temple, Puri.

• Jharkhand (Option 3): A mineral-rich eastern state carved out of Bihar in 2000, home to archer Deepika Kumari.

• Assam (Option 4): A north-eastern state famous for tea, one-horned rhinoceros and the Brahmaputra river.

question: SPREE 2025 is a special initiative aimed at _____ under the Employees' State Insurance (ESI) Act.
option_1: providing housing support to middle-income families
option_3: launching health insurance for gig workers
option_4: extending pension benefits to state employees
solution_text:
The correct answer is expanding social security coverage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• SPREE 2025 stands for Scheme to Promote Registration of Employers/Employees, launched by the ESIC (Employees' State Insurance Corporation).

• Its aim is expanding social security coverage (सामाजिक सुरक्षा कवरेज का विस्तार) by encouraging registration of left-out employers and workers under the ESI Act.

• The scheme was active from 1 July to 31 December 2025.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The ESIC functions under the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

• Registered employees get medical, sickness, maternity, disablement and dependents' benefits.

NOTE

• Providing housing support to middle-income families (Option 1): Not the aim of SPREE; housing is handled by schemes like PMAY.

• Launching health insurance for gig workers (Option 3): Gig-worker welfare is addressed separately, e.g. under the e-Shram/Code on Social Security.

• Extending pension benefits to state employees (Option 4): Pension matters relate to EPFO/state schemes, not SPREE.

question: In May 2025, who has been appointed as the Chief Justice of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai (न्यायमूर्ति भूषण रामकृष्ण गवई) was sworn in as the 52nd Chief Justice of India on 14 May 2025.

• He is the second Dalit and the first Buddhist to hold the office of CJI.

• He succeeded Justice Sanjiv Khanna.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The CJI is appointed by the President under Article 124 of the Constitution.

• The senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is conventionally appointed as the CJI.

NOTE

• Justice D.Y. Chandrachud (Option 1): Was the 50th CJI of India (2022–2024).

• Justice U.U. Lalit (Option 3): Was the 49th CJI of India in 2022.

• Justice N.V. Ramana (Option 4): Was the 48th CJI of India (2021–2022).

question: Former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao was posthumously awarded the _____ in 2024.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharat Ratna.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Former PM P.V. Narasimha Rao was posthumously conferred the Bharat Ratna (भारत रत्न) in 2024.

• As Prime Minister (1991–1996) he initiated India's economic liberalisation (LPG reforms) and is often called the 'Father of Indian Economic Reforms'.

• In 2024 the Bharat Ratna was also given to Karpoori Thakur, L.K. Advani, Chaudhary Charan Singh and M.S. Swaminathan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award, instituted in 1954.

• It is awarded for exceptional service in any field of human endeavour.

NOTE

• Padma Vibhushan (Option 2): India's second-highest civilian award.

• Padma Bhushan (Option 3): India's third-highest civilian award.

• Gandhi Peace Prize (Option 4): An annual award for social, economic and political transformation through non-violence.

question: In July 2025, The Youth Spiritual Summit culminated in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Varanasi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Youth Spiritual Summit culminated in Varanasi (वाराणसी), Uttar Pradesh, in July 2025 with the launch of the 'Kashi Declaration'.

• The summit promoted the 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat' (drug-free youth) movement.

• It was held from 18 to 20 July 2025.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Varanasi (Kashi) is one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities, situated on the banks of the Ganga.

• It is the parliamentary constituency of PM Narendra Modi.

NOTE

• Surat (Option 2): A city in Gujarat known as the diamond and textile hub of India.

• Ujjain (Option 3): A temple city in Madhya Pradesh on the Shipra river, a Kumbh Mela site.

• Madurai (Option 4): A temple city in Tamil Nadu famous for the Meenakshi Amman Temple.

question: Which law replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (भारतीय न्याय संहिता), 2023 replaced the colonial-era Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860.

• It is the main criminal (substantive) law of India, effective from 1 July 2024.

• The three new criminal laws replaced the IPC, CrPC and Indian Evidence Act.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The BNS has 358 sections and introduced new offences like organised crime and mob lynching.

• The three new laws were passed by Parliament in December 2023.

NOTE

• Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 (Option 2): Replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973.

• Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023 (Option 3): Replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.

• Nyaya Danda Adhiniyam, 2023 (Option 4): A fictitious/non-existent law name.

question: The India Innovation Index is released by NITI Aayog and _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Institute for Competitiveness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The India Innovation Index is released by NITI Aayog in partnership with the Institute for Competitiveness (प्रतिस्पर्धात्मकता संस्थान).

• It ranks Indian states and union territories on their innovation capabilities and ecosystems.

• The first edition was launched in 2019.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.

• In earlier editions, Karnataka topped the major states category.

NOTE

• CSIR (Option 2): Council of Scientific and Industrial Research, India's premier R&D organisation.

• Ministry of Education (Option 3): The central ministry handling school and higher education.

• Reserve Bank of India (Option 4): India's central bank and monetary authority.

question: In July 2024, the National Landslide Forecasting Centre was inaugurated at _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kolkata.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Landslide Forecasting Centre (राष्ट्रीय भूस्खलन पूर्वानुमान केंद्र) was inaugurated at Kolkata in July 2024.

• It was set up by the Geological Survey of India (GSI), headquartered in Kolkata.

• It issues daily landslide forecasts for vulnerable regions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Geological Survey of India (GSI) was founded in 1851 and functions under the Ministry of Mines.

• Landslide forecasting initially covers states like Nilgiris, Darjeeling and Kalimpong.

NOTE

• Patna (Option 1): Capital of Bihar, an ancient city (Pataliputra) on the Ganga.

• Bhopal (Option 3): Capital of Madhya Pradesh, known as the 'City of Lakes'.

• Raipur (Option 4): Capital of Chhattisgarh.

question: The Aravalli Green Wall Project aims to spread green cover in the buffer area around the Aravalli range in _____ districts of four states.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 29.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Aravalli Green Wall Project (अरावली ग्रीन वॉल परियोजना) aims to spread green cover in a 5 km buffer around the Aravalli range across 29 districts of four states.

• The four states are Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Delhi.

• It was launched in 2023 and is inspired by Africa's Great Green Wall.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Aravalli range is one of the oldest fold mountain systems in the world.

• The project aims to combat land degradation and desertification.

NOTE

• 10 (Option 1): Incorrect number of districts for the project.

• 19 (Option 2): Incorrect number of districts for the project.

• 70 (Option 4): Incorrect number of districts for the project.

question: Which of the following Assamese songs is a 'lullaby'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nichukoni-geet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nichukoni-geet (निसुकोनी-गीत) is the traditional Assamese lullaby sung to put children to sleep.

• 'Nichukoni' means to lull or soothe a child.

• Such songs are part of Assam's rich folk-music tradition.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Assamese folk songs are broadly linked with festivals, work and life-cycle rituals.

• The most famous Assamese folk songs are the Bihu-geet, associated with the Bihu festival.

NOTE

• Bihu-geet (Option 1): Folk songs sung during the Bihu festival of Assam.

• Bon-geet (Option 2): A category of Assamese folk songs (forest/field songs).

• Biyanaam (Option 3): Assamese marriage/wedding songs.

question: Around which year did the construction of the Red Fort in Delhi began?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1639.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The construction of the Red Fort (लाल किला) in Delhi began around 1639 under Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.

• It was completed in 1648 and became the seat of Mughal power at Shahjahanabad.

• It was designed by the architect Ustad Ahmad Lahori.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Red Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2007).

• Every year on Independence Day, the Prime Minister hoists the national flag here.

NOTE

• 1605 (Option 1): The year Emperor Akbar died and Jahangir ascended the throne.

• 1622 (Option 2): Not linked to the Red Fort's construction.

• 1658 (Option 4): The year Aurangzeb ascended the Mughal throne.

question: In which Indian state is the folk-dance form 'Terah Taali' traditionally performed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Terah Taali (तेरह ताली) is a folk dance traditionally performed in Rajasthan.

• It is performed by the Kamad community in devotion to folk deity Baba Ramdev.

• Women dancers tie thirteen manjiras (small cymbals) to their bodies and strike them rhythmically.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other famous folk dances of Rajasthan include Ghoomar, Kalbelia and Bhavai.

• Kalbelia dance of Rajasthan is on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list.

NOTE

• Jharkhand (Option 2): Known for folk dances like Chhau, Paika and Jhumar.

• Kerala (Option 3): Known for Kathakali, Mohiniyattam and Theyyam.

• Odisha (Option 4): Known for the classical Odissi and the Gotipua dance.

question: Europa Clipper is the first mission designed to conduct a detailed study of _____'s moon Europa.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jupiter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Europa Clipper is NASA's mission to study Jupiter's (बृहस्पति) moon Europa in detail.

• Europa is believed to have a subsurface ocean of liquid water beneath its icy crust, making it a candidate for life.

• The mission was launched in October 2024.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system and a gas giant.

• Its four largest (Galilean) moons are Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto.

NOTE

• Mars (Option 1): The 'Red Planet', with moons Phobos and Deimos.

• Saturn (Option 3): The gas giant famous for its ring system; largest moon is Titan.

• Uranus (Option 4): An ice giant that rotates on its side.

question: Which space agency operates the CryoSat satellite, designed to study polar ice thickness and monitor climate change?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ESA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The CryoSat satellite is operated by the European Space Agency (ESA / ई.एस.ए.).

• It is designed to measure polar ice thickness and monitor changes in ice sheets and sea ice due to climate change.

• CryoSat-2 was launched in 2010.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• ESA is an intergovernmental organisation of European nations, established in 1975, headquartered in Paris.

• CryoSat carries a radar altimeter (SIRAL) to measure ice elevation.

NOTE

• NASA (Option 1): The US space agency (National Aeronautics and Space Administration).

• ISRO (Option 2): The Indian Space Research Organisation, headquartered in Bengaluru.

• JAXA (Option 3): The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency.

question: The Government introduced the 'Navratna' scheme in _____ to identify and support CPSEs with competitive advantages in their journey to becoming global leaders.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1997.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Government introduced the 'Navratna' (नवरत्न) scheme in 1997 to grant greater operational and financial autonomy to selected profit-making CPSEs (Central Public Sector Enterprises).

• The aim was to help these companies become global giants.

• The initial list included companies like IOC, ONGC, SAIL, BHEL, etc.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Categories of CPSEs include Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna.

• The Maharatna category was introduced later in 2010.

NOTE

• 2001 (Option 1): Not the year the Navratna scheme was introduced.

• 1993 (Option 2): Not the year the Navratna scheme was introduced.

• 1999 (Option 3): Not the year the Navratna scheme was introduced.

question: Who among the following was the Governor-General of British India from 1773 to 1785?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Warren Hastings.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Warren Hastings (वॉरेन हेस्टिंग्स) was the first Governor-General of Bengal/British India (1773–1785).

• He was appointed under the Regulating Act of 1773.

• He established the Asiatic Society of Bengal (1784) with William Jones.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• He faced impeachment proceedings in the British Parliament, but was finally acquitted.

• During his tenure the Treaty of Salbai (1782) ended the First Anglo-Maratha War.

NOTE

• Lord Wellesley (Option 2): Governor-General (1798–1805), introduced the Subsidiary Alliance system.

• Lord Dalhousie (Option 3): Governor-General (1848–1856), introduced the Doctrine of Lapse and railways.

• Lord Cornwallis (Option 4): Governor-General who introduced the Permanent Settlement (1793).

question: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act was enacted in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2003.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act (राजकोषीय उत्तरदायित्व और बजट प्रबंधन अधिनियम) was enacted in 2003.

• It aims to ensure fiscal discipline by reducing the fiscal deficit and eliminating the revenue deficit.

• It became effective from 2004.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The FRBM Act promotes long-term macroeconomic stability and transparency in fiscal operations.

• The N.K. Singh Committee was set up to review the FRBM Act.

NOTE

• 2007 (Option 1): Not the year the FRBM Act was enacted.

• 2001 (Option 2): The year the FRBM Bill was first introduced in Parliament, but not enacted.

• 2005 (Option 4): Not the year the FRBM Act was enacted.

question:
Which of the following mineral is found in the Himalayan mineral belt of India?
I. Copper
II. Tungsten
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Himalayan mineral belt (हिमालय खनिज बेल्ट) contains both Copper and Tungsten.

• This belt extends along the Himalayan mountain ranges of northern India.

• It also contains minerals like cobalt, nickel and precious stones.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India's major mineral belts include the North-Eastern Peninsular belt, Central belt, Southern belt and the Himalayan belt.

• Copper is a good conductor used in electrical wiring; Tungsten has the highest melting point of all metals.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, since Tungsten is also found in the Himalayan belt.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, since Copper is also found in the Himalayan belt.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both minerals are found in the belt.

question: What was the density of India in per square km as per census 1951?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 117.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of 1951, the population density of India was 117 persons per square km.

• Population density = total population / total land area.

• It has risen steadily to 382 per sq km in the 2011 Census.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The 1951 Census was the first census conducted after India's independence.

• The census in India is conducted every 10 years by the Office of the Registrar General.

NOTE

• 77 (Option 1): Not the density recorded in the 1951 Census.

• 97 (Option 2): Not the density recorded in the 1951 Census.

• 217 (Option 4): Not the density recorded in the 1951 Census.

question: Who was the Chairperson of the Planning Commission when it was formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jawaharlal Nehru (जवाहरलाल नेहरू) was the first Chairperson of the Planning Commission, which was formed in 1950.

• The Prime Minister is the ex-officio Chairperson of the Planning Commission.

• The Planning Commission was a non-constitutional, non-statutory body.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015.

• The First Five Year Plan (1951–56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model.

NOTE

• Morarji Desai (Option 2): India's fourth Prime Minister (1977–1979).

• Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel (Option 3): India's first Home Minister and Deputy PM, the 'Iron Man of India'.

• K Kamraj (Option 4): Former Chief Minister of Madras State and Congress leader (Kamaraj Plan).

question: Which of the following five year plan of India commenced at a time when the global economy was going through a second financial crisis?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Twelfth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Twelfth Five Year Plan (बारहवीं, 2012–2017) commenced when the global economy was passing through a second financial crisis (after 2008).

• Its theme was 'Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth'.

• It was the last Five Year Plan of India before the plan system was discontinued.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Twelfth Plan targeted an average annual GDP growth of around 8%.

• After 2017, Five Year Plans were replaced by NITI Aayog's Vision documents.

NOTE

• First (Option 1): The First Plan (1951–56) focused on agriculture and irrigation.

• Third (Option 2): The Third Plan (1961–66) was disrupted by wars and drought.

• Fourth (Option 3): The Fourth Plan (1969–74) emphasised growth with stability and self-reliance.

question:
Which of the following is an example of Administration town in India?
I. Shillong
II. Chandigarh
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both Shillong and Chandigarh are examples of administrative towns (प्रशासनिक शहर) in India.

• Administrative towns are those whose primary function is government administration, usually as capital cities.

• Shillong is the capital of Meghalaya, and Chandigarh is the capital of Punjab and Haryana.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Towns are classified by function as administrative, industrial, transport, commercial, mining, garrison and educational towns.

• Other administrative towns include New Delhi, Gandhinagar and Bhopal.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, since Chandigarh is also an administrative town.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, since Shillong is also an administrative town.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, since both are administrative towns.

question: What structures are provided in the upper part of the respiratory tract to remove germs, dust, and other harmful particles from inhaled air in humans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cilia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cilia (सिलिया) are tiny hair-like structures in the upper respiratory tract that trap and remove germs, dust and harmful particles from inhaled air.

• Along with mucus, they form the mucociliary escalator that sweeps trapped particles out of the airways.

• They help keep the lungs clean and free from infection.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The nasal cavity also contains hair and mucus that filter incoming air.

• The respiratory tract also warms and moistens the air before it reaches the lungs.

NOTE

• Alveoli (Option 1): Tiny air sacs in the lungs where exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide occurs.

• Bronchi (Option 2): The two main airways branching from the trachea into the lungs.

• Pleura (Option 3): The double-layered membrane covering the lungs.

question: Which of the following sense is detected by gustatory receptors?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Taste.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gustatory receptors detect the sense of Taste (स्वाद).

• These receptors are located in the taste buds on the tongue.

• The five basic tastes are sweet, sour, salty, bitter and umami.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Olfactory receptors detect smell, and the two senses (taste and smell) work together to give flavour.

• Taste buds are found in the papillae on the surface of the tongue.

NOTE

• Sight (Option 1): Detected by photoreceptors (rods and cones) in the retina of the eye.

• Smell (Option 2): Detected by olfactory receptors in the nasal cavity.

• Hearing (Option 4): Detected by receptors (hair cells) in the cochlea of the inner ear.

question: Which Vedic text category explains mantras and sacrificial rituals in prose form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmanas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Brahmanas (ब्राह्मण) are the Vedic texts that explain the mantras and sacrificial rituals (yajnas) in prose form.

• They serve as prose commentaries attached to each of the four Vedas, detailing the procedures of sacrifices.

• Examples include the Aitareya Brahmana and the Shatapatha Brahmana.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Each Veda has four parts: Samhitas, Brahmanas, Aranyakas and Upanishads.

• The four Vedas are Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda.

NOTE

• Samhitas (Option 1): The core collections of hymns and mantras of the Vedas.

• Aranyakas (Option 2): 'Forest texts' dealing with rituals, ceremonies and their philosophy.

• Upanishads (Option 4): Philosophical texts (Vedanta) dealing with metaphysics and self-realisation.
